title: Certificates always seem to expire on weekends
excerpt: An expired certificate is a calendar problem dressed up as a security one. Three habits that keep it boring.
body:
An expired TLS certificate is a calendar problem dressed up as a security problem. Nothing is broken until, suddenly, everything is.

Three habits I now treat as non-negotiable:

- **Automate renewal, then monitor the automation.** A renewal job that fails silently is worse than no job, because everyone believes it works.
- **Alert on days remaining, not on failure.** Thirty days of warning is a ticket. Zero days is an incident.
- **Keep an inventory.** If you can't list every certificate you own and where it lives, you'll find out about one from an angry user.

None of this is clever. That's the point: the goal is for renewal to be boring.
